SYN-PUB-07001.title: Time-domain simulation of conducted disturbances generated by single-phase rectifiers in low-voltage residential networks
SYN-PUB-07001.text:
Time-domain simulation of conducted disturbances generated by single-phase rectifiers in low-voltage residential networks (2010, journal, Serbian Journal of Electrical Engineering).
Authors: Miroslav Čabarkapa (outside co-author); Đorđe Petrović (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: conducted emissions; time-domain simulation; single-phase rectifier; LISN; low-voltage network.
A time-domain simulation framework is developed to predict conducted emissions from single-phase uncontrolled rectifiers connected to a simplified residential low-voltage network. The network is represented by a ladder model with frequency-dependent line parameters derived from measurements on a 230 V, 50 Hz test feeder of approximately 120 m length. Rectifier loads ranging from 100 W to 2 kW are modelled as nonlinear voltage-dependent current sources parameterised from laboratory measurements. Simulated disturbance voltages at the mains terminal are compared against LISN-based measurements following CISPR 16-1-1 procedures over the 9 kHz to 30 MHz range. Agreement within 4 dB is achieved across the 150 kHz to 2 MHz sub-band, with larger deviations at higher frequencies attributed to parasitic capacitances not included in the ladder model. The study identifies the 450 kHz to 600 kHz interval as the most sensitive to load power level, with peak quasi-peak levels increasing by up to 11 dB when aggregate load increases from 500 W to 2 kW. The results suggest that existing CISPR limits may be approached under dense residential loading conditions.

SYN-PUB-07002.title: Frequency-dependent impedance characterisation of low-voltage cable types used in Serbian urban distribution networks
SYN-PUB-07002.text:
Frequency-dependent impedance characterisation of low-voltage cable types used in Serbian urban distribution networks (2011, conference, Proceedings of the 8th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology (EMCEE), Belgrade).
Authors: Tatjana Kovačević (outside co-author); Luca Marchetti (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: cable impedance; frequency-dependent parameters; transmission-line model; SPICE; conducted emission.
The per-unit-length impedance and admittance parameters of four cable types commonly deployed in Serbian urban low-voltage distribution networks are characterised over the 10 kHz to 30 MHz frequency range using a two-port vector network analyser. Cable lengths between 10 m and 80 m are measured in open-circuit and short-circuit configurations, and results are fitted to a standard transmission-line model augmented with a skin-effect correction term. Measured propagation constants are compared to values predicted by IEC 60228-based geometric calculations, revealing deviations of up to 18% in the attenuation constant above 1 MHz for flat-conductor aluminium cables. The characterised parameters are incorporated into a SPICE-compatible model library intended for conducted emission simulations. Sensitivity analysis shows that uncertainty in conductor geometry translates to a maximum 6 dB uncertainty in predicted disturbance voltage at a 30 m cable termination at 10 MHz. The data set covers NYY, NAYY, NYM and NYFGbY cable types in cross-sections from 1.5 mm² to 25 mm².

SYN-PUB-07003.title: Impact of variable-speed drives on harmonic voltage distortion in industrial low-voltage busbars
SYN-PUB-07003.text:
Impact of variable-speed drives on harmonic voltage distortion in industrial low-voltage busbars (2013, journal, Electrical Power Systems Research).
Authors: Aleksandar Simić (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611); Bojan Ristić (outside co-author).
Keywords: harmonic distortion; variable-speed drives; power quality; harmonic load flow; EN 50160.
Harmonic voltage measurements are carried out on three low-voltage industrial busbars (400 V, 50 Hz) in a metalworking facility over a seven-day continuous recording period using a class A power quality analyser. Variable-speed drives of 5.5 kW to 90 kW nameplate ratings account for between 40% and 70% of connected load depending on the shift schedule. Total harmonic distortion of voltage (THDV) consistently exceeds the EN 50160 indicative limit of 8% during peak production hours, reaching up to 12.3%. The fifth and seventh voltage harmonics dominate, with average magnitudes of 4.1% and 3.6% of fundamental respectively. Measured current spectra from individual drives are used to construct aggregated injection models following IEC 61000-3-6 guidelines, and harmonic load flow calculations are performed on a network model validated against field measurements. Simulations reproduce measured THDV values within 1.5 percentage points. Mitigation options including passive fifth-harmonic filters and increased feeder conductor cross-section are evaluated, with the former reducing THDV to below 6% under peak load.

SYN-PUB-07004.title: Conducted emission test reproducibility for switch-mode power supplies: influence of LISN topology and mains impedance variation
SYN-PUB-07004.text:
Conducted emission test reproducibility for switch-mode power supplies: influence of LISN topology and mains impedance variation (2014, journal, IEEE Transactions on Electromagnetic Compatibility).
Authors: Klaus Hoffmeister (outside co-author); Miroslav Čabarkapa (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: LISN; CISPR 32; switch-mode power supply; test reproducibility; mains impedance.
Switch-mode power supplies (SMPS) are tested for conducted emissions according to CISPR 32 using three commercially available line impedance stabilisation networks (LISNs) of nominally identical 50 Ω/50 µH topology but from different manufacturers. Tests are performed on five SMPS samples with rated power between 30 W and 250 W. Measured quasi-peak levels at the same SMPS unit differ by up to 7.2 dB across LISNs in the 150 kHz to 500 kHz band, exceeding the 3 dB reproducibility figure often cited in the literature. The observed discrepancies are traced to differences in the LISN high-frequency impedance characteristic, particularly a self-resonance near 1.4 MHz in one unit. An additional test campaign varies the mains source impedance from 0.05 Ω to 0.8 Ω at 50 Hz by inserting series inductors, demonstrating that SMPS peak emission levels shift by up to 5 dB due to changes in rectifier operating point. These findings have implications for compliance margins and for the interpretation of borderline-pass test results.

SYN-PUB-07005.title: Interference between ripple control signals and supraharmonic emissions in distribution networks: a time-domain case study
SYN-PUB-07005.text:
Interference between ripple control signals and supraharmonic emissions in distribution networks: a time-domain case study (2018, journal, International Journal of Electrical Power and Energy Systems).
Authors: Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Gábor Fekete (outside co-author); Nataša Vuković (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: ripple control; supraharmonics; interference; time-domain model; distribution network.
Ripple control systems operating at 316.7 Hz and 750 Hz are widely used by distribution system operators in central Europe for remote load switching. This study investigates the extent to which supraharmonic emissions from switch-mode loads corrupt ripple control telegram reception in a 400 V test feeder modelled from parameters measured in a suburban distribution area near Novi Sad. A full time-domain model is built in MATLAB/Simulink incorporating a ripple control transmitter, feeder impedance, and four classes of switching loads: SMPS, LED drivers, PV micro-inverters, and EV on-board chargers. At 15% feeder loading with mixed loads, signal-to-interference ratio at the receiver input drops below the 20 dB design threshold assumed in EN 61000-5-1 for ripple control. Worst-case degradation of 28 dB is observed when multiple PV micro-inverters synchronise their switching near the ripple control frequency. Temporal correlation between load power cycles and interference bursts is demonstrated. The model is validated against a 4-hour measurement record from the test feeder with 4.5% mean absolute error in receiver input voltage.

SYN-PUB-07006.title: Common-mode and differential-mode separation of conducted emissions: measurement method comparison and uncertainty analysis
SYN-PUB-07006.text:
Common-mode and differential-mode separation of conducted emissions: measurement method comparison and uncertainty analysis (2019, journal, Metrology and Measurement Systems).
Authors: Miroslav Čabarkapa (outside co-author); Ida Lerch (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: common mode; differential mode; conducted emissions; measurement uncertainty; LISN.
Four methods for separating common-mode (CM) and differential-mode (DM) conducted emissions from single-phase equipment are compared: a commercial CM/DM separator, a home-built balun-based separator, a two-LISN simultaneous measurement approach, and a post-processing technique applied to standard LISN recordings. Measurements are performed on five reference loads including a 100 W SMPS, a 40 W LED driver array, and a 1.5 kW motor controller in the 150 kHz to 30 MHz band. Separator insertion loss and balance-to-unbalance conversion ratio are characterised by network analyser, revealing that the commercial unit maintains 40 dB mode separation only below 5 MHz. Uncertainty budgets are constructed according to JCGM 100:2008 for each method. Total standard uncertainty ranges from 1.1 dB to 3.8 dB depending on method and frequency, with the two-LISN method providing the lowest uncertainty above 10 MHz. Practical guidance is provided on method selection depending on available equipment and required accuracy.

SYN-PUB-07008.title: Conducted disturbance propagation from EV on-board chargers: network impedance dependency and phase-to-phase coupling
SYN-PUB-07008.text:
Conducted disturbance propagation from EV on-board chargers: network impedance dependency and phase-to-phase coupling (2021, journal, IEEE Transactions on Power Delivery).
Authors: Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Jasmina Jokić (R0769); Marta Johansson (outside co-author); Tatjana Kovačević (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: EV charger; conducted emissions; three-phase feeder; phase coupling; charging infrastructure.
Three-phase low-voltage feeders serving residential parking areas with electric vehicle charging infrastructure are studied using a combination of laboratory measurements and network simulation. On-board chargers of 3.3 kW, 7.4 kW and 11 kW rated power are characterised individually on a LISN test bench, and their emission spectra exported as Norton equivalent sources. A three-phase feeder model of 60 m length is parameterised from field impedance measurements and loaded with up to 12 simultaneous charger connections distributed across phases. Phase-to-phase coupling via the neutral conductor and earth return path is analysed and shown to introduce cross-phase disturbance voltages up to 8 dB below the directly driven phase in the 150 kHz to 500 kHz band. Feeder impedance variation due to the connection of reactive compensation capacitors shifts dominant emission peaks by up to 40 kHz. Compliance margins relative to EN 61000-3-11 group emission limits shrink by 6 dB when six or more chargers of the same type operate simultaneously. Results are discussed in the context of planned charging hub deployments.

SYN-PUB-07010.title: Statistical characterisation of supraharmonic emission levels in a low-voltage feeder over a 12-month monitoring campaign
SYN-PUB-07010.text:
Statistical characterisation of supraharmonic emission levels in a low-voltage feeder over a 12-month monitoring campaign (2023, journal, Electric Power Systems Research).
Authors: Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Rossella Fantozzi (outside co-author); Gábor Fekete (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: supraharmonics; long-term monitoring; statistical characterisation; low-voltage feeder; lognormal distribution.
Continuous monitoring of supraharmonic current and voltage emissions at the 400 V low-voltage busbar of a suburban distribution substation near Novi Sad is carried out over twelve consecutive months using a purpose-built acquisition system with 1 MS/s sampling and 90 dB dynamic range. The feeder supplies a mixture of residential and small commercial loads. Emission spectra are computed in 200 Hz bins from 2 kHz to 150 kHz on a ten-minute aggregation basis in accordance with the draft measurement protocol of IEC/TR 61000-2-1-2 Ed.2. Statistical distributions of emission levels are fitted to lognormal models at selected spectral bins; the 95th percentile levels at 16 kHz and 40 kHz are 12.1% and 6.3% of the fundamental current respectively. Clear diurnal and weekly patterns are observed, with evening peaks 4 to 9 dB above overnight minima. Seasonal variation is modest (less than 2 dB) except at 16 kHz, where a 5 dB increase in winter is attributed to increased LED and SMPS loading. The data set is made available as a supplementary repository and is intended for validation of aggregation models.

SYN-PUB-07794.title: Steady-State Voltage Profile Analysis in Radial Low-Voltage Feeders with Rooftop Photovoltaic Systems
SYN-PUB-07794.text:
Steady-State Voltage Profile Analysis in Radial Low-Voltage Feeders with Rooftop Photovoltaic Systems (2013, conference, Proceedings of the International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications, Osijek).
Authors: Aleksandar Jeremić (R0696); Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Miroslav Stanić (outside co-author).
Keywords: voltage profile; radial feeder; backward-forward sweep; photovoltaic; EN 50160.
This paper presents a steady-state power flow analysis of a 0.4 kV radial distribution feeder in an urban residential area of Novi Sad, incorporating measured generation profiles from twelve rooftop photovoltaic installations aggregating 48 kWp of installed capacity. A backward–forward sweep load flow algorithm was implemented and validated against one week of SCADA measurements. Voltage profiles were computed under three penetration scenarios: 20 %, 50 %, and 80 % of feeder customers operating as prosumers. Results indicate that reverse power flow emerges at penetration levels above 35 % under peak irradiance conditions, causing end-of-feeder voltage to exceed the EN 50160 upper limit of 1.10 p.u. for approximately 4.2 % of annual hours at 80 % penetration. The sensitivity of voltage rise to feeder impedance ratio X/R was quantified, showing that resistive-dominant cables characteristic of low-voltage grids amplify voltage deviations by a factor of 1.6 compared to equivalent medium-voltage lines. The study provides a benchmark dataset and simulation framework subsequently used in follow-up hosting capacity work.

SYN-PUB-07795.title: Reactive Power Compensation Using Fixed Capacitor Banks in Distribution Feeders with Variable Generation: A Sensitivity Study
SYN-PUB-07795.text:
Reactive Power Compensation Using Fixed Capacitor Banks in Distribution Feeders with Variable Generation: A Sensitivity Study (2015, journal, Serbian Journal of Electrical Engineering).
Authors: Aleksandar Jeremić (R0696); Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Katarina Blagojević (outside co-author).
Keywords: reactive power compensation; capacitor banks; power factor; voltage constraint; Vojvodina.
Fixed shunt capacitor banks remain common in Serbian low-voltage distribution infrastructure. This paper evaluates their effectiveness under variable photovoltaic generation using a sensitivity analysis approach applied to a representative 0.4 kV test feeder parameterised from field measurements in the Vojvodina region. Thirty-two daily generation profiles collected over two seasons were used as input. Power factor correction was assessed at three placement positions along the feeder, and the interaction between capacitor injection and reverse power flow was examined. The analysis shows that fixed capacitor banks installed at the mid-feeder position reduce reactive power import by 22 % on average but cause overvoltage exceedances of up to 0.04 p.u. during midday peak generation periods, a finding that is absent in purely passive feeder conditions. The paper quantifies the trade-off between power factor improvement and voltage constraint violation as a function of installed photovoltaic capacity, providing practical guidelines for distribution system operators considering retrofit compensation strategies without active voltage control.

SYN-PUB-07796.title: Hosting Capacity Assessment for Photovoltaic Systems in Low-Voltage Urban Networks: Deterministic and Stochastic Approaches Compared
SYN-PUB-07796.text:
Hosting Capacity Assessment for Photovoltaic Systems in Low-Voltage Urban Networks: Deterministic and Stochastic Approaches Compared (2018, journal, Electric Power Systems Research – Balkan Regional Edition).
Authors: Aleksandar Jeremić (R0696); Miroslav Stanić (outside co-author); Tibor Farkaš (outside co-author); Ivana Jović (outside co-author).
Keywords: hosting capacity; Monte Carlo; deterministic assessment; urban feeder; prosumer connection.

SYN-PUB-07797.title: Smart Inverter Volt–Var Control for Voltage Regulation in Prosumer-Integrated Low-Voltage Feeders
SYN-PUB-07797.text:
Smart Inverter Volt–Var Control for Voltage Regulation in Prosumer-Integrated Low-Voltage Feeders (2020, journal, IET Renewable Power Generation).
Authors: Aleksandar Jeremić (R0696); Luka Petrović (outside co-author); Andrea Rossi (outside co-author); Miroslav Stanić (outside co-author).
Keywords: smart inverter; Volt-VAr control; Q(U) characteristic; hardware-in-the-loop; RTDS.
Grid-connected photovoltaic inverters with programmable Volt–VAr (Q(U)) characteristic functions can absorb or inject reactive power in response to local voltage measurements, providing a distributed voltage regulation mechanism without centralised communication. This paper implements and tests three Q(U) characteristic shapes—linear, piecewise linear with deadband, and cosφ(P)—on a hardware-in-the-loop test bench using an RTDS real-time simulator interfaced with a commercial 5 kW single-phase inverter. Feeder parameters replicate a 380 m urban cable section. Simulations and hardware experiments were conducted for 120 irradiance scenarios generated from one year of meteorological data for Novi Sad. The piecewise linear characteristic with a ±2 % voltage deadband reduces voltage violations at the feeder end by 87 % compared to unity power factor operation while increasing inverter reactive current by no more than 18 % of rated current. Additional reactive losses of 1.1 % of annual energy yield are recorded, representing the compensation cost. The experimental setup and parameter tuning procedure are described in sufficient detail for replication.

SYN-PUB-07798.title: Impact of Electric Vehicle Charging on Voltage Quality and Hosting Capacity in Residential Low-Voltage Feeders
SYN-PUB-07798.text:
Impact of Electric Vehicle Charging on Voltage Quality and Hosting Capacity in Residential Low-Voltage Feeders (2021, conference, Proceedings of the IEEE International Energy Conference, Split).
Authors: Ivana Jović (outside co-author); Aleksandar Jeremić (R0696); Nenad Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: electric vehicle charging; hosting capacity; voltage quality; stochastic modelling; residential feeder.
The simultaneous rollout of rooftop photovoltaics and private electric vehicle (EV) charging in residential areas creates competing and sometimes complementary effects on feeder voltage profiles. This paper extends an existing hosting capacity framework to include EV load as a stochastic variable characterised by charging start time, state-of-charge on arrival, and rated charger power. Input distributions were estimated from a mobility survey of 340 respondents in the greater Novi Sad area conducted in 2019. Three charging strategies are compared: uncontrolled immediate charging, night-valley charging, and solar-matched daytime charging. Results on a 0.4 kV feeder model show that uncontrolled charging during evening hours reduces hosting capacity by up to 9 kWp relative to the no-EV baseline because voltage drop from EV load adds to end-of-feeder sag during low-generation periods, restricting the permissible generation envelope. Daytime solar-matched charging, by contrast, partially offsets voltage rise and increases median hosting capacity by 6 kWp. The paper identifies feeder impedance as the dominant factor moderating these interactions.

SYN-PUB-07799.title: Feeder Reconfiguration as a Hosting Capacity Enhancement Tool in Meshed Low-Voltage Networks
SYN-PUB-07799.text:
Feeder Reconfiguration as a Hosting Capacity Enhancement Tool in Meshed Low-Voltage Networks (2023, journal, Electric Power Systems Research).
Authors: Miroslav Stanić (outside co-author); Aleksandar Jeremić (R0696); Ivana Jović (outside co-author).
Keywords: feeder reconfiguration; normally-open point; meshed network; hosting capacity; impedance balancing.
Low-voltage distribution networks in newer urban developments in Serbia are built with a meshed cable topology but operated radially through normally-open points. Switching the normally-open point changes feeder lengths, impedance distributions, and load sharing, all of which affect hosting capacity for distributed generation. This study systematically evaluates feeder reconfiguration as a low-cost hosting capacity enhancement measure for a 0.4 kV meshed network of 84 nodes representing a residential district in Novi Sad. A brute-force enumeration of all 12 candidate normally-open point positions is combined with the stochastic hosting capacity assessment method from previous work. Results show that the optimal normally-open point configuration raises the network-wide hosting capacity by 23 % compared to the default as-built configuration, without any hardware investment. The improvement is driven primarily by impedance balancing across two parallel cable routes. The sensitivity of results to load growth assumptions of 1 % and 2 % annual increase is also reported, showing that reconfiguration benefits persist over a 10-year horizon under both scenarios.

SYN-PUB-07800.title: Battery Storage Sizing for Voltage Support in Low-Voltage Feeders: A Cost–Benefit Approach
SYN-PUB-07800.text:
Battery Storage Sizing for Voltage Support in Low-Voltage Feeders: A Cost–Benefit Approach (2024, journal, Journal of Energy Storage).
Authors: Luka Petrović (outside co-author); Aleksandar Jeremić (R0696); Andrea Rossi (outside co-author); Stefan Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: battery storage; sizing optimisation; voltage support; prosumer; cost-benefit analysis.
Behind-the-meter battery energy storage systems can flatten prosumer net load profiles and provide reactive power support to the local feeder. This paper addresses the problem of selecting storage capacity and power rating to maximise a combined economic and technical objective consisting of prosumer electricity bill reduction, avoided distribution system operator penalty costs for voltage violations, and degradation cost of the battery over a 10-year planning horizon. A mixed-integer linear programming formulation is developed and applied to four prosumer archetypes derived from clustering 18 months of smart meter data collected from 210 customers in Novi Sad. Storage sizes in the range 3–12 kWh are evaluated with lithium iron phosphate chemistry. Results indicate that economically optimal storage sizes for the studied archetypes fall between 4.5 kWh and 7 kWh, constrained primarily by battery degradation cost rather than voltage benefit. Sensitivity to electricity tariff structure shows that time-of-use tariffs with a peak-to-off-peak ratio above 2.4 significantly shift optimal sizes upward.

SYN-PUB-07801.title: Probabilistic Hosting Capacity Maps for Low-Voltage Distribution Networks: A Methodology for Municipal-Scale Assessment
SYN-PUB-07801.text:
Probabilistic Hosting Capacity Maps for Low-Voltage Distribution Networks: A Methodology for Municipal-Scale Assessment (2025, journal, IEEE Transactions on Power Delivery).
Authors: Aleksandar Jeremić (R0696); Stefan Kovačević (outside co-author); Cristina Moldovan (outside co-author); Tibor Farkaš (outside co-author); Nenad Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: hosting capacity mapping; probabilistic assessment; feeder classification; municipal scale; spatial analysis.
Distribution system operators and municipal planners require spatially aggregated information on available photovoltaic hosting capacity to guide permitting decisions and grid investment planning. This paper proposes a methodology for producing probabilistic hosting capacity maps at the level of an entire municipal distribution network by applying a stratified feeder sampling approach. Feeders are classified into six morphological types based on cable length, cross-section, and customer density. For each type, 500 stochastic hosting capacity assessments are performed. The resulting per-type distributions are spatially assigned to all 1 140 low-voltage feeders in a medium-sized municipality in the Vojvodina region, producing a rasterised map with 100 m resolution. The map is validated against 23 actual photovoltaic connection applications processed by the distribution system operator in 2022–2023, showing that 91 % of accepted connections fell within the predicted feasible range. Limitations of the stratification approach and data requirements from the distribution system operator are discussed in detail.

SYN-PUB-08181.title: Baseline Performance Ratio Modelling for Grid-Connected PV Systems Using Ordinary Least Squares Regression on One-Year SCADA Logs
SYN-PUB-08181.text:
Baseline Performance Ratio Modelling for Grid-Connected PV Systems Using Ordinary Least Squares Regression on One-Year SCADA Logs (2014, journal, Journal of Renewable Energy Systems and Monitoring).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Marija Vučković (outside co-author); Dragan Ilić (outside co-author).
Keywords: performance ratio; PV baseline; OLS regression; SCADA; degradation.
This paper presents a regression-based methodology for constructing performance ratio (PR) baselines for grid-connected photovoltaic installations using twelve months of five-minute SCADA records from a 2.4 MWp ground-mount park in Vojvodina. Ordinary least squares models were fitted separately for each inverter string, with irradiance, ambient temperature, and wind speed as predictors. The residual time series were then examined for systematic drift, which was taken as a proxy for gradual degradation. The fitted models explained between 91 % and 96 % of PR variance across sixteen inverter strings. A cross-validation scheme based on seasonal stratification was used to assess generalisation. Results showed that simple linear models are competitive with more complex approaches when training data cover at least eight months and include summer irradiance peaks. Limitations related to sensor calibration drift and curtailment events are discussed in detail.

SYN-PUB-08182.title: Early Fault Classification in Photovoltaic String Inverters Using Random Forest on SCADA-Derived Statistical Features
SYN-PUB-08182.text:
Early Fault Classification in Photovoltaic String Inverters Using Random Forest on SCADA-Derived Statistical Features (2018, journal, Journal of Industrial Condition Monitoring and Diagnostics).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Nemanja Petrović (outside co-author); Ágnes Kovács (outside co-author); Radovan Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: fault classification; random forest; string inverter; SCADA features; domain shift.
Inverter faults in distributed PV installations often produce subtle signatures in current and voltage telemetry before they result in full failure or protection trip. This paper extracts a set of 34 statistical features—including rolling mean, standard deviation, skewness, and crossing-rate measures—from five-minute SCADA records of eleven string inverters monitored over three years at two sites in Serbia. A random forest classifier trained on labelled fault events—covering IGBT degradation, grid relay issues, and sensor faults—achieved macro-averaged F1 of 0.81 on held-out data when a detection window of 48 hours before the logged fault event was used. Permutation importance analysis identified AC-side current imbalance and temperature-normalised efficiency drop as the two most informative features. The trained model was tested on a third site without retraining to assess domain shift, yielding an acceptable F1 of 0.73.

SYN-PUB-08183.title: Anomaly Scoring for District Heating Substation Telemetry Using Isolation Forest with Temporal Resampling
SYN-PUB-08183.text:
Anomaly Scoring for District Heating Substation Telemetry Using Isolation Forest with Temporal Resampling (2020, journal, Energy and Buildings Automation Journal).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Bojana Marković (outside co-author); Tomáš Novák (outside co-author).
Keywords: isolation forest; district heating; anomaly scoring; seasonal baseline; telemetry.
District heating substations generate continuous telemetry—supply and return temperatures, flow rate, differential pressure, valve position—that reflects both normal load variation and incipient faults. This paper applies isolation forest anomaly scoring to hourly-resampled records from 38 substations in a mid-sized Serbian city, covering two full heating seasons. To reduce the influence of strong daily and weekly periodicity, features were constructed as deviations from a Fourier-smoothed seasonal baseline rather than raw sensor values. Anomaly scores were validated against a maintenance log containing 54 confirmed fault events, yielding precision of 0.69 and recall of 0.78 at the chosen score threshold. False positives were predominantly associated with demand-side events such as building renovations. The paper also discusses operational considerations for deploying the pipeline in the control room of a heat utility, where interpretability requirements constrain model complexity.

SYN-PUB-08184.title: Comparison of Univariate and Multivariate LSTM Architectures for Remaining Useful Life Prediction in PV Inverters
SYN-PUB-08184.text:
Comparison of Univariate and Multivariate LSTM Architectures for Remaining Useful Life Prediction in PV Inverters (2021, conference, Proceedings of the Balkan Workshop on Machine Learning in Energy Systems (BWMLES)).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Nemanja Petrović (outside co-author); Milica Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: LSTM; remaining useful life; PV inverter; attention mechanism; label noise.
Recurrent neural networks have been proposed for remaining useful life (RUL) estimation in power electronics, but the benefit of multivariate input over simpler univariate temperature-tracking models is not always clear in practice. This study compares four LSTM configurations—single-channel temperature, three-channel electrical, full nine-channel SCADA, and a multivariate model with attention—trained on labelled degradation sequences collected from 23 inverters across four sites over four years. RUL ground truth was derived from inverter replacement records. The univariate temperature model achieved mean absolute error of 18.3 days; the full nine-channel model with attention reduced this to 11.7 days. However, the improvement was statistically significant only for IGBT-related failures, not for capacitor or relay faults. Training data size, label noise from opportunistic rather than condition-triggered replacements, and class imbalance are examined as confounding factors.

SYN-PUB-08185.title: Transfer Learning for PV Fault Detection Across Geographically Distributed Sites with Different Inverter Brands
SYN-PUB-08185.text:
Transfer Learning for PV Fault Detection Across Geographically Distributed Sites with Different Inverter Brands (2022, journal, Renewable Energy Monitoring and Diagnostics).
Authors: Andrei Moldovan (outside co-author); Marija Vučković (outside co-author); Igor Starčević (R0738); Radovan Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: transfer learning; fault detection; PV; gradient boosting; cross-site generalisation.
Training fault detection models independently for each PV installation is data-expensive and impractical for small or newly commissioned sites. This paper investigates fine-tuning a source-domain random forest and a gradient-boosted tree, both pre-trained on five Serbian PV sites, using small labelled batches from two Romanian target sites with different inverter brands and monitoring intervals. Fine-tuning with as few as 30 labelled target-domain fault windows raised F1 from a zero-shot baseline of 0.48 to 0.74 for the random forest and to 0.77 for the gradient-boosted model. Feature alignment using quantile normalisation per sensor channel proved more effective than raw standardisation. The study uses publicly documented fault taxonomies and consistent labelling criteria to enable reproducibility, and the pre-trained model weights are made available with the paper.

SYN-PUB-08186.title: Threshold Selection Strategies for Operational Anomaly Detection Pipelines in Industrial SCADA Environments
SYN-PUB-08186.text:
Threshold Selection Strategies for Operational Anomaly Detection Pipelines in Industrial SCADA Environments (2023, journal, Journal of Industrial Data Science and Process Monitoring).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Ágnes Kovács (outside co-author).
Keywords: threshold selection; anomaly detection; SCADA; cost-sensitive; operational deployment.
Most anomaly detection research reports performance at a single fixed threshold chosen post-hoc to maximise a validation metric, which does not reflect operational reality where false alarm rates carry real costs. This paper surveys and empirically compares six threshold selection strategies—fixed percentile, precision–recall curve knee-point, F-beta optimisation, cost-sensitive selection, control-chart 3-sigma rule, and manual operator calibration—applied to isolation forest and autoencoder anomaly scores on SCADA telemetry from two PV parks and one wind farm. Data cover 36 months and 112 documented fault events. Cost-sensitive selection with an asymmetric cost matrix calibrated by an operator survey consistently outperformed fixed-percentile approaches across all three sites, reducing total operational cost by 19–34 % compared to the 95th-percentile baseline. The paper provides a decision workflow for practitioners choosing among strategies given available labelled data and operator input.

SYN-PUB-08187.title: Autoencoder-Based Detection of Sensor Drift in Long-Running PV Monitoring Systems
SYN-PUB-08187.text:
Autoencoder-Based Detection of Sensor Drift in Long-Running PV Monitoring Systems (2025, journal, Sensors and Instrumentation for Industrial Monitoring).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Nemanja Petrović (outside co-author); Andrei Moldovan (outside co-author).
Keywords: autoencoder; sensor drift; PV monitoring; hardware-in-the-loop; reconstruction error.
Irradiance and temperature sensors deployed in field PV monitoring stations drift gradually due to soiling, ageing, and mechanical misalignment, introducing systematic bias into SCADA telemetry that is difficult to distinguish from true plant degradation. This paper trains a convolutional autoencoder on the first twelve months of records from twelve monitoring stations, treating this period as nominally calibrated, and then monitors reconstruction error on subsequent 36 months of data. Three types of drift—irradiance pyranometer zero-offset, temperature sensor gain shift, and voltage divider ageing—were induced artificially in a hardware-in-the-loop testbed to generate labelled validation data. The autoencoder flagged all three drift types within a two-week detection lag at an average false positive rate of 8 %. A lightweight rule-based filter using interquartile consistency across co-located sensors reduced false positives to 3 % without increasing the detection lag. The method was subsequently applied to two production archives where unconfirmed drift events were identified.

SYN-PUB-08188.title: Benchmarking Time-Series Foundation Models Against Classical Methods for Short-Horizon Anomaly Detection in Energy SCADA Telemetry
SYN-PUB-08188.text:
Benchmarking Time-Series Foundation Models Against Classical Methods for Short-Horizon Anomaly Detection in Energy SCADA Telemetry (2026, preprint, arXiv preprint).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Srđan Kovačević (outside co-author); Bojana Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: foundation models; benchmarking; anomaly detection; SCADA; edge deployment.
Large pre-trained time-series models have been proposed as general-purpose tools that can be applied to downstream tasks with little or no fine-tuning. This paper benchmarks three recently published time-series foundation models against four classical methods—isolation forest, one-class SVM, ARIMA residual scoring, and a simple rolling z-score—on anomaly detection tasks drawn from five SCADA datasets covering PV parks, a small wind farm, and district heating substations. Evaluation uses a consistent labelling protocol and the same six threshold selection strategies described in earlier work by the same group. Foundation models achieved the highest AUC-ROC on two of the five datasets but were outperformed by isolation forest on the remaining three, particularly where telemetry channels exhibit strong non-stationary seasonality. Inference latency and memory footprint are also reported, as they are relevant constraints for edge deployment in substation hardware.

SYN-PUB-09619.title: Day-ahead PV forecasting for distribution feeders with satellite cloud data
SYN-PUB-09619.text:
Day-ahead PV forecasting for distribution feeders with satellite cloud data (2024, journal, Renewable Grid Integration).
Authors: Tamara Simić (R0904); Milena Đorđević (outside co-author); Kristijan Varga (outside co-author); Andrei Moldovan (outside co-author).
This paper presents a day-ahead photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting methodology for distribution feeders that integrates high-resolution satellite cloud motion imagery with numerical weather prediction data. The proposed framework applies a hybrid convolutional–recurrent neural network architecture to extract spatiotemporal cloud patterns and translate them into irradiance estimates at feeder level. Case studies are conducted on five medium-voltage distribution feeders in Vojvodina, covering a cumulative installed PV capacity of approximately 18 MW. The model is benchmarked against persistence, smart persistence, and a standard multilayer perceptron baseline. Results demonstrate a reduction of 17–23% in normalised root mean square error compared with the best-performing baseline across all test feeders. Probabilistic forecast intervals derived via conformal prediction are also evaluated using coverage and sharpness metrics. The methodology is designed to support intraday dispatch decisions by distribution system operators (DSOs) seeking to accommodate high shares of behind-the-meter solar generation while maintaining voltage profiles within statutory limits.

SYN-PUB-09620.title: Demand response potential of industrial consumers in Vojvodina
SYN-PUB-09620.text:
Demand response potential of industrial consumers in Vojvodina (2022, conference, European Energy Markets Conference).
Authors: Bojan Kostadinović (outside co-author); Vesna Ilić (outside co-author); Tamara Simić (R0904); Dragana Petrović (outside co-author).
Industrial consumers represent a largely untapped source of demand-side flexibility in South-East European electricity systems. This paper quantifies the demand response (DR) potential of manufacturing and agri-food processing facilities located in the Vojvodina region of Serbia through a combination of on-site energy audits, smart meter time-series analysis, and structured interviews with energy managers. Flexible loads are categorised by response speed, duration, and recovery constraints, yielding a total dispatchable capacity of 47 MW across the surveyed sample. The analysis reveals that refrigeration systems, compressed-air networks, and irrigation pumps collectively account for more than 60% of the identified flexibility. Barriers to market participation are examined, including the absence of a formalised balancing market product compatible with small aggregators and limited metering infrastructure at sub-hourly resolution. Policy recommendations are offered for aligning Serbian regulatory frameworks with EU demand response directives, and a roadmap for pilot aggregator programmes is outlined. The findings are directly relevant to distribution system operators and the emerging flexibility procurement landscape in the Western Balkans.

SYN-PUB-09621.title: Probabilistic short-term load forecasting with gradient boosting
SYN-PUB-09621.text:
Probabilistic short-term load forecasting with gradient boosting (2021, journal, Journal of Energy Forecasting).
Authors: Tamara Simić (R0904); Nemanja Vuković (outside co-author); Szabolcs Fekete (outside co-author); Aleksandra Marinović (outside co-author).
Accurate probabilistic short-term load forecasting (STLF) is essential for efficient energy scheduling, reserve dimensioning, and distribution network planning. This paper proposes a probabilistic STLF framework based on gradient boosting regression trees augmented with quantile loss functions, enabling simultaneous estimation of multiple prediction intervals without parametric distributional assumptions. A comprehensive feature engineering pipeline incorporates lagged consumption values, calendar effects, temperature dew-point interactions, and holiday indicators derived from Serbian public calendars. The model is trained and validated on two years of hourly active power measurements from 12 distribution substations supplied by a regional DSO in northern Serbia. Probabilistic calibration is assessed using the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) and reliability diagrams across 10%, 50%, and 90% quantiles. The gradient boosting approach outperforms Gaussian process regression and quantile random forests on CRPS by margins of 8–14%, while maintaining sub-second inference times suitable for operational deployment. Practical guidance for hyperparameter tuning and rolling-window retraining schedules is also discussed.

SYN-PUB-09622.title: Intraday solar irradiance nowcasting using sky-imager optical flow for urban distribution networks
SYN-PUB-09622.text:
Intraday solar irradiance nowcasting using sky-imager optical flow for urban distribution networks (2023, journal, Solar Energy and Power Systems Journal (fictional)).
Authors: Tamara Simić (R0904); Milena Đorđević (outside co-author); Róbert Szabó (outside co-author); Ivan Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: irradiance nowcasting; sky imager; optical flow; PV forecasting; distribution network.
Very short-term solar irradiance nowcasting is critical for real-time balancing of distribution networks with high rooftop PV penetration. This paper introduces an optical-flow-based nowcasting method that processes sequences of ground-level sky images captured at one-minute intervals by a network of low-cost all-sky cameras installed across the city of Novi Sad. Cloud motion vectors are estimated using a pyramidal Lucas–Kanade algorithm and projected onto a ground irradiance map via a geometric sky-to-plane transformation. The resulting irradiance field is aggregated to feeder level and evaluated against pyranometer measurements and smart inverter telemetry. Forecast horizons of 5, 15, and 30 minutes are examined. The optical flow model reduces mean absolute error by 21% relative to a persistence baseline at the 15-minute horizon. Uncertainty quantification is incorporated through an ensemble of perturbed optical flow fields, producing calibrated prediction intervals. Results demonstrate that sky-imager networks can complement satellite-based products and provide actionable nowcasts for DSO control room operators managing curtailment and reactive power compensation in real time.

SYN-PUB-09623.title: Flexibility aggregation framework for residential prosumers in Serbian distribution grids
SYN-PUB-09623.text:
Flexibility aggregation framework for residential prosumers in Serbian distribution grids (2023, conference, International Conference on Smart Energy Systems and Technologies – SEST 2023 (fictional proceedings)).
Authors: Bojan Kostadinović (outside co-author); Tamara Simić (R0904); Lidija Marković (outside co-author); Christoph Reiner (outside co-author).
Keywords: flexibility aggregation; prosumer; virtual power plant; distribution system operator; demand response.
The proliferation of rooftop solar panels, home battery storage, and smart appliances is creating a new category of residential prosumers capable of providing grid flexibility services. However, aggregating small distributed resources into market-ready products remains technically and contractually complex, particularly in regulatory environments that have not yet fully transposed EU Clean Energy Package provisions. This paper proposes a hierarchical aggregation framework tailored to the Serbian distribution context, in which a virtual power plant (VPP) operator coordinates prosumer flexibility bids submitted to a day-ahead local flexibility market operated by the DSO. A mixed-integer linear programming dispatch model accounts for prosumer comfort constraints, battery state-of-charge limits, and network congestion thresholds. The framework is validated through a simulation study on a realistic 34-bus low-voltage feeder parameterised with data from a pilot neighbourhood in Novi Sad. Results show that coordinated prosumer dispatch reduces peak feeder loading by 18% while delivering measurable economic benefits to participants. Regulatory gaps and recommended amendments to Serbian energy bylaws are discussed.

SYN-PUB-09624.title: Transfer learning for PV power forecasting across climate zones in the Western Balkans
SYN-PUB-09624.text:
Transfer learning for PV power forecasting across climate zones in the Western Balkans (2022, journal, Applied Energy Modelling (fictional journal)).
Authors: Nemanja Vuković (outside co-author); Andrei Moldovan (outside co-author); Marija Bjelić (outside co-author); Tamara Simić (R0904).
Keywords: transfer learning; PV forecasting; domain adaptation; Western Balkans; renewable integration.
Building accurate machine learning forecasting models for photovoltaic installations typically requires extensive historical generation data, which is unavailable for newly commissioned plants. Transfer learning offers a principled approach to knowledge reuse across sites with differing climatic and topographic characteristics. This study investigates domain adaptation strategies for day-ahead PV power forecasting across seven sites spanning the Western Balkans, representing Mediterranean, continental, and highland climate zones. A source-domain model pre-trained on a data-rich coastal site is fine-tuned using limited target-domain data through three transfer protocols: full network fine-tuning, feature extraction with frozen convolutional layers, and adversarial domain adaptation. Performance is assessed using normalised RMSE and skill score relative to smart persistence. Adversarial domain adaptation achieves the best generalisation with as few as 30 days of target-site observations, reducing normalised RMSE by up to 19% compared with a model trained from scratch on the same limited dataset. The results have practical implications for DSOs and project developers commissioning new solar farms where historical data are scarce.

SYN-PUB-09625.title: Congestion management in active distribution networks through DSO-operated local flexibility markets
SYN-PUB-09625.text:
Congestion management in active distribution networks through DSO-operated local flexibility markets (2024, journal, IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid (fictional)).
Authors: Tamara Simić (R0904); Vesna Ilić (outside co-author); Aleksandra Marinović (outside co-author); Pieter van den Berg (outside co-author).
Keywords: local flexibility market; congestion management; active distribution network; optimal power flow; DSO.
Active distribution networks with significant renewable generation increasingly face congestion events that traditional grid reinforcement cannot address cost-effectively in the short term. Local flexibility markets (LFMs) operated by distribution system operators offer an alternative mechanism in which prosumers and aggregators submit bids to resolve specific network constraints. This paper presents an LFM clearing algorithm based on an optimal power flow formulation with linearised branch flow equations, designed to accommodate the computational constraints of DSO operational systems. The algorithm is embedded within a co-simulation platform coupling a distribution grid model with an agent-based market simulator. Three congestion scenarios are evaluated on a 69-bus synthetic network calibrated to reflect a peri-urban feeder topology typical of northern Serbia. Comparative analysis against classical curtailment orders demonstrates that the LFM approach reduces total flexibility procurement costs by 31% on average while maintaining voltage and thermal compliance. Scalability to real DSO systems and interoperability with national balancing market products are discussed in the context of forthcoming Serbian grid code revisions.

SYN-PUB-09627.title: Smart metering data analytics for non-technical loss detection in Serbian distribution feeders
SYN-PUB-09627.text:
Smart metering data analytics for non-technical loss detection in Serbian distribution feeders (2020, journal, IET Smart Grid (fictional journal)).
Authors: Tamara Simić (R0904); Nemanja Vuković (outside co-author); Szabolcs Fekete (outside co-author); Jovana Ristić (outside co-author).
Keywords: non-technical loss detection; smart metering; anomaly detection; random forest; distribution system operator.
Non-technical losses (NTL) arising from electricity theft and meter tampering represent a significant financial burden for distribution system operators in South-East Europe, with estimates suggesting NTL rates of 4–9% in parts of Serbia. Advanced metering infrastructure deployments are generating large volumes of smart meter data that, if properly analysed, can provide early detection signals for NTL events. This paper develops a supervised anomaly detection pipeline that combines feature extraction from half-hourly consumption profiles—including load shape indices, phase imbalance ratios, and night-time baseload metrics—with a random forest classifier trained on labelled NTL incidents documented by a regional DSO. The classifier is augmented with a SHAP-based explainability module to assist field inspection teams in prioritising investigation visits. A retrospective study on 4,200 metering points over 18 months demonstrates a true positive rate of 78% at a false positive rate of 5%, substantially outperforming the DSO's existing rule-based detection system. The approach is designed to integrate with standard DSO SCADA and meter data management architectures without requiring proprietary data formats.

W3177274304.title: Comparison of Reactive Power Control Techniques for Solar PV Inverters to Mitigate Voltage Rise in Low-Voltage Grids
W3177274304.text: Electronics, 2021. The greater integration of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems into low-voltage (LV) distribution networks has posed new challenges for the operation of power systems. The violation of voltage limits attributed to reverse power flow has been recognized as one of the significant consequences of high PV penetration. Thus, the reactive power control of PV inverters has emerged as a viable solution for localized voltage regulation. This paper presents a detailed study on a typical Malaysian LV distribution network to demonstrate the effectiveness of different reactive power control techniques in mitigating overvoltage issues due to high PV integration. The performance of four reactive power control techniques namely, fixed power factor control, scheduled power factor control, power factor control as a function of injected active power, and voltage-dependent reactive power control were analyzed and compared in terms of the number of customers with voltage violations, reactive power compensation, and network losses. Three-phase, time-series, high-resolution power-flow simulations were performed to investigate the potential overvoltage issues and to assess the performance of the adoption of reactive power controls in the network. The simulation results revealed that the incorporation of reactive power controls of solar PV inverters aids in successfully mitigating the overvoltage issues of typical Malaysian networks. …
